This page is for contributors to `scgsim.geometry`. It records how a
`GeometryPlan` turns its sources into the normalized input SGB builds from, and
which records travel in the snapshot. What a user calls, and what each call
accepts, is on [GeometryPlan and SGB](../../reference/specs/geometry-plan.qmd).

## Source authorities {#source-authorities}

The in-tree `scgsim.geometry` API is SCGSim's source-geometry authority. It
reads structured PDK and component semantics and never reconstructs geometry
meaning from solver-generated labels. `scgsim.geometry` is the source-facing
facade: `GeometryPlan`, detached snapshots, normalized input models, adapters,
stack, vacuum and curve preparation, and summaries. Palace builds the geometry
with `scgsim.geometry.sgb` (`build_sgb_geometry`) and meshes it with
`scgsim.meshing`. The source validator is `scgsim.geometry.source.validation`.

`GeometryPlan` composes two authorities. PDK `LayerStack` records supply
materials, process layers, Z and thickness, conductor and solution roles, and
host volumes. Component annotations supply local Entity identity, ports,
functional conductor regions and topology selectors. The notebook composes
named occurrences and assigns the final Net map; it does not author PDK or
component facts.

The
[physical representation contract](../../reference/specs/physical-representation.qmd) separates
source physical classification from selected solver representation. One neutral
plan binds each original Entity and physical layer to its effective geometry,
support and complete enclosure trace. A body retains its actual source
endpoints and holes; a nominal layer span is not a replacement body. Missing
qualified contact or host incidence remains absent rather than inferred.

Palace and AEDT consume the same chosen interpretation. Different explicit
profiles retain their different approximation meanings; source attachment
normals do not decide native HFSS field-side selection. Historical recorded
source and runtime cohorts retain their original interpretation and identity.

## Grid noding and the change ledger {#grid-noding}

`GeometryPlan` and `build_gds_stack_geometry_input(...)` take the grid from
the GDS they read: its database unit, `source_dbu_um`, is the shared layout
grid. SCGSim reads the DBU and does not mutate shared PDK or global state.
`metadata.geometry_grid` records `schema_version` with value
`scgsim.geometry.grid.v1`, the grid's `grid_size_um`, and `coordinate_frame`
with value `assembly_xy`. It identifies the shared fixed-precision grid for
assembly XY/layer arrangement. Every later stage reads the grid from it; an
input without `metadata.geometry_grid` is refused with a `ValueError` that names
the two calls which declare it. Original source identity is retained alongside the
computational change ledger, and walls inherit their snapped layout endpoints.
Z coordinates, film thickness, mesh, quadrature, and solver tolerances remain
separate; the XY grid does not assert that every 3D coordinate lies on it.
The fixed-grid XY boundaries are noded once for each Z range. A Z range's
network holds every operand whose closed Z range meets that range, touching
included, and every operand that has no Z range; operands whose Z ranges are
separated never share nodes. A bump that spans the D0-to-D1 gap is therefore
noded with the metal of both dies, while a D1 vertex does not split a D0
outline. One limit follows from this grouping: when a D0 conductor and a bump
share an edge and a D1 vertex lies on it, the bump outline gets that vertex
and the D0 outline does not. Within each network, every original directed ring
edge carries its operand, ring and segment order through explicit grid-pixel
incidence; coincident edges retain every source. Raw intersection and
native-grid near-vertex events split these directed paths before rounding.

Directed edge transitions determine face membership, and each operand is reconstructed
from those same cells without another grid snap. Ambiguous source paths or
inconsistent labels fail explicitly. Source recipes round flattened layout
points to the grid before their Booleans, so a mask placed through a rotated
reference and drawn again directly unions to one outline. Physical contact,
hole and component checks still compare against the original, unrounded
inputs.

## Source occurrence records {#source-occurrence-records}

For component-semantics schema v2, the paired stack adds derived source
occurrence records, not a new user polygon-selection API. Each
`metadata.source_occurrences` row binds a registered path and parent path to a
cell name, composed transform, and `reference_index`: the zero-based reference
ordinal in that parent, or `null` for the root. One registered occurrence names
one actual GDS reference. Consumers must first expand arrays into explicit
individual references; `GeometryPlan` does not auto-expand arrays. Each layer's
`geometry.source_occurrence_polygons_um` and each
`metadata.port_sheet_source_layers` entry's `source_occurrence_polygon_um`
preserve selected exterior and hole loops in micrometres. The reader checks
the paired GDS hash, binds each path to its recorded parent reference and child
cell, converts the source database units, reapplies the composed transform,
and recomputes those loops. This keeps touching same-layer geometry from
separate named occurrences distinct. Existing schema-v1 stack readers keep
their selector decoding behavior.

## Ground-plane contributions {#ground-plane-contributions}

In the public Xmon composition, the reusable child keeps its local pad,
coupler, mask, and a ground-arm metal contribution. That arm overlaps the
residual ground plane, so it is not a separate conductor Entity; modeling it
as one would duplicate metal. The root composition supplies one D0 and one D1
plane through the stack recipe, then unions the occurrence-local arm geometry
into the D1 plane through an explicit physical conductor-layer binding; the
draw or mask layer does not imply that target. It does not copy full
ground-plane Entities into each child occurrence or create planes
automatically.

Component-semantics v2 also accepts
`component_semantics.ground_plane_contributions`. Each record has exactly
`local_id`, `plane_id`, `level`, `layer`, and `selector_point_um`. The local ID
names a component-local metal contribution; `plane_id` names a root-local
derived plane. `level` is the physical conductor level and must match the
target plane's `metadata.logical_layer_id`; `layer` is the source GDS
layer/datatype pair used with the local selector point. Thus a draw or mask
layer does not implicitly choose the target conductor face.

Preparation uses the selector to resolve one connected occurrence-local metal
region on the declared source GDS layer. That region can contain multiple
fused raw GDS polygons. The root-plane and occurrence paths use the same local
plane/mask/include geometry recipe. GeometryPlan applies the occurrence
transform once, verifies the resulting exterior and hole loops against the
paired GDS, and records them in the root plane's
`geometry.source_occurrence_includes`. The root plane's
`metadata.ground_plane_contribution_sources` retains the occurrence path, local
ID, physical level, and source layer. A selected region that contains a
separately declared local conductor on the same physical level is rejected.
These includes become part of the residual plane before polygon lowering; they
are not separate conductor Entities or Net assignments, and GeometryPlan does
not infer connectivity or promise separate measurements.

## Rectangular junction derivation {#rectangular-junction-derivation}

The shared geometry interpreter derives the complete central rectangle and
terminal-owned end metals once, from the source database units and existing
physical attachment, before planning contacts, interfaces, and construction
catalogues. Palace Route A continues to apply its existing
host-interface, common-plane, and common-volume rules. Palace and AEDT consume
the same derived source partition; AEDT validates that request rather than
deriving another rectangle. Palace `add_port(...)` still binds inductance to an
authored port name and does not choose the physical terminal owners.

## The source-to-backend contract in full {#source-contract-table}

| Fact or operation | Contract |
|---|---|
| Component definition | Holds local polygons, source Entity IDs, ports, topology selectors, and local component facts. Reusing a component does not rewrite its local IDs. Schema v2 does not assign final Nets or expose a public `Group` API inside the component. |
| Component occurrence | `register_instance(path, reference)` binds a named path to the actual GDSFactory occurrence. Parent segments are registered before children. The path scopes entity and polygon identities before flattening; rotation and reflection apply consistently to geometry, selectors, and ports. |
| Notebook net mapping | Authors only the final `Net -> Entity` map on the `GeometryPlan`; components do not carry intermediate or child net assignments. Membership may be assigned once to one net; duplicate membership on the same net is deduplicated. There is no public component `Group` API, implicit connectivity, or child-net merge framework. |
| Assignment validation | Mapping updates are atomic. Unknown or ambiguous entity references and an entity assigned across different nets reject the whole update. An unmapped entity remains unassigned (`None`); a backend requires a net binding only where that backend operation needs one. |
| Source lineage | The immutable snapshot preserves source Entity and polygon identities separately from derived group membership. An Entity is lineage, not a promise of a raw per-Entity measurement or field expression. A `semantic_group_id` is not reused as Entity identity or source lineage. |
| Computational groups | New physical mesh grouping serves high-count geometry only. Copies may share one computational physical group when explicit Net, material, local source Entity ID, parent occurrence context, and role all match. Qualified Entity/member lineage remains available; an unassigned Net stays separate. For example, the eight sibling Ground bumps in this coupon map to one physical group while retaining eight Entity IDs. Legacy recorded physical-group policy remains version-specific. AEDT owner/interface/integral groups remain backend-specific and keep their existing policy. |
| Backend lowering | Palace and AEDT consume the same prepared source snapshot through their existing preparation paths. Native aggregates retain their source members and coverage. This does not promise per-patch native results, per-Entity raw measurements, or per-Entity field expressions. |
| Vacuum geometry | Authored vacuum entities keep their names, materials, hosts, and per-domain analysis identity. At the source-input level, the plan adds one outer background domain as the semantic complement of modeled bodies and custom regions under the established SGB priority/cut rules. The backend owns how it represents that partition natively. The public `D0_TO_D1_GAP` remains a distinct vacuum entity. |
| AEDT object names | New native names are readable and deterministic, sanitized and disambiguated as needed, and remain bound to the original qualified Entity ID. Historical prepared names keep their version-specific reader policy. |
| Boundary defaults | Palace leaves an unspecified external vacuum boundary at its natural PMC condition. HFSS assigns the same condition, Perfect H, on the faces of its Region. |

Source preparation establishes
the geometry input contract; it does not imply native geometry validation or
solver execution.

## Q3D source normalization {#accepted-q3d-source-normalization}

The Q3D GeometryPlan frontend is part of the public API. Its recognized `airbridge_deck`
and `airbridge_post` records remain role-neutral source
geometry in the normalized snapshot; they are not given a Palace route
representation or a native conductor role by normalization. A selected Palace
route continues to reject conductors it cannot represent. AEDT Q3D solves
the SGB model of the snapshot, with its final caller-authored Net membership
and explicit physical ground roles; authored arcs reach it as exact arcs in the
model's STEP. This source contract does not assert completion of a Q3D
solve or returned matrix observation.

## Curve construction {#curve-construction}

SGB builds the declared lines and circular arcs into one exact planar
arrangement on the integer grid, extrudes it over the authored stack, and writes
the BREP and XAO files itself; it runs no OCC Boolean and no shell repair. Each
face keeps its source identity in the sidecar, and Gmsh only opens the written
XAO to check it before meshing. A construction error stops the build; there is
no straight-edge fallback or volume repair.

Geometry order and finite element order are separate choices. Curved model
geometry does not make a positive surface inset an exact curved-perimeter
distance; see the
[EPR interpretation](../../concepts/surface-epr.qmd#surface-identity-masks-and-loss-assumptions).

## Internal semantic projection {#internal-semantic-projection}

SGB projects already-validated source facts once per source/model revision into
`scgsim.semantics`. The immutable projection is reused while planning a model;
it is not rebuilt by deep-copying a full stack for every interface pair.
Interface classification and each owner projection remain distinct operations:
solution solid/vacuum ordering is not interchangeable with declared surface
owners, legacy two-owner records, sheet owners, or aggregate physical-group
owners.

The projection can express finite PEC, surface-sheet MA/MS, local MM/MA patch
evidence, explicit side meaning, and outer/hole/seam provenance without
claiming that classification proves contact. Declared, planned, and observed
records remain distinguishable. Native tags and groups are opaque observations,
not reconstructed successes, and duplicate observations do not multiply one
semantic contribution.

Explicit authored interface kind and owner metadata take precedence
over derived defaults. Route-A sheet contact footprints remain an `MM`
topology relation but lower as the existing `MS` cap with its established
physical-name prefix; the surrounding sheet may still carry its independently
classified MA/MS evidence.

Route-A profile selection is optional for a direct semantic-core consumer.
A Palace simulation on Route A without a profile uses `thin_film`
(`set_route("A")`); `substrate_face` or `metal_gap_equivalent` with their film
bindings are passed as `set_route("A", approximation_profile=...)`. Route B
without a profile uses the identity profile `route_b`. With no core profile, coordinates remain unchanged and no collapse is
recorded. `metal_gap_equivalent` remains the existing effective coordinate
normalization; no reversible-collapse claim is made.

For a stack with no PDK vacuum layer, omitted conductor host declarations are
bound to the internally generated background only when the caller selects
`plan.set_vacuum_region()`. The same normalized polygon-versus-substrate-region
contact check supplies Route-A physical support for both authored-host and
generated-background stacks. It considers complete exteriors and holes and
requires a unique positive-area contact; a bounding-box intersection,
point/edge touch, or auto-region edge is insufficient. An authored
but unresolved host name still fails instead of being silently rebound.
Single-substrate `substrate_face` has no opposing die or gap value; two
opposed substrates keep physical `substrate_face` and the distinct
two-face-only `metal_gap_equivalent` normalization. The generated Region is
profiled after the source geometry and partitioned around actual dielectric
and finite-PEC occupancy. Route-A sheets do not subtract a fictitious volume.

Route-A support is local rather than a whole-sheet label. The sheet polygon is
partitioned by exact bottom/top solution coverage before bare SA/AA surfaces
are constructed, so substrate holes remain holes and a partly supported stress
case retains separate supported and exposed children. Each child keeps ordered
bottom/top evidence; an MM contact cap retains only the side left after the
contact cut. Port footprints select the intersecting child and fail if they
cross incompatible local domain pairs. Fully freestanding sheets remain
unsupported.

The same local-domain partition is used when conductor faces are removed from
an SA patch. The planner subtracts only the face overlap with that exact
solution-pair patch, even when one conductor spans several adjacent domains.

Route B keeps finite geometry and records local top, bottom, and sidewall
material-side evidence. Geometry adjacency remains a set, whereas the additive
contribution ledger preserves semantic multiplicity. Two same-kind MA sides
on one Route-A child share one native surface and one aggregate Palace row;
they are not duplicated or multiplied. That aggregate requires Palace's
internal-boundary cracking and does not imply side-resolved numeric output.
AEDT reads its Surface-EPR rows from the sidecar of the same SGB model.

## Identity requirements {#identity-requirements}

A handoff preserves:

- source SGB revision;
- semantic surface and volume identities;
- route choice and topology receipt;
- generated mesh/config identity;
- the mapping from solver entities back to semantic geometry.

## Shared source facts for AEDT {#shared-source-facts-for-aedt}

`GeometryPlan` is the shared source frontend for Palace and AEDT. Its prepared
snapshot includes the normalized `GeometryBuildInput` polygons (including
hole loops), entities, solution regions, source provenance, and route profile,
along with the prepared stack and source-occurrence records. Source-linked
junction declarations retain their terminal nets, direction, dimensions,
inductance, and capacitance; those fields are not retroactively attributed to
the normalized `GeometryBuildInput`. AEDT builds the SGB model of the
snapshot with `prepare_sgb_model` and imports its STEP; it takes object names,
face groups and Surface-EPR rows from that model's sidecar and guard, not from
Gmsh surfaces, physical groups or native tags.

The run checks what AEDT imported against the guard: every object and face must
match the model's sidecar and guard, or the run stops. A native face overlap or
adjacency query is observed geometry evidence; it cannot manufacture source
contact intent. Route-A profile normalization still happens once at the shared
frontend boundary.

## Preparation pool and caches {#preparation-resources}

The scope reuses one pool for independent source recipes, indexed source-path
batches, zero-area support classification and per-operand reconstruction.
Results and task-local source audits merge in input order. Fixed-grid operands
share the same boundary network and labelled cells; source-path ownership and
face transitions remain deterministic. Unquantized parent planes keep their
separate construction path. Nested work reuses the budget rather than creating
another pool. Preparation tasks finish before the meshing child processes
start. Meshing runs on one Gmsh thread, so it takes no share of the worker budget;
the scope only keeps it out of a preparation worker.

Each source-preparation call also reuses hierarchy extraction for the same
freshly read GDS cell and excluded-reference list. The cache ends with that
call.

Immutable raw polygons and pure subdivisions are also reused within a prepare,
or adapter call when the complete ordered operands and grid context
match. Selectors,
source-record comparisons and physical/contact audits still execute on each
invocation.

Reconstructed grid-applied faces use one coordinate
representation per integer grid key, including their boundary-chain anchors;
raw source coordinates and non-grid local planes remain separate.

A topology
failure retains its original exception and adds counts, validity, area and
grid information without coordinates. Error-only witnesses distinguish the
initial grid realization, labelled cells and reconstructed faces from the
final shared-cell reconstruction. These witnesses do not replace the model or
its checks.

## Input summary display {#pre-solve-input-summary}

`scgsim.geometry.summarize_geometry_input(build_input, *, prepared_stack)` returns an
`InputSummary` with detached `.data` and an HTML representation for notebook
display. Both Eigenmode facades and `ElectrostaticSim` expose `input_summary()`
to combine this normalized source with their configured backend settings. AEDT summarizes its
normalized build input and stack. Palace requires its bound `GeometryPlan` and
summarizes the input its `mesh()` prepares from that plan, so the plan's vacuum
region, the ports set on the simulation and the route's conductor
representation appear as the model will have them.
Passing a raw component without explicit normalization fails rather than
guessing a stack. The summary records source, entity, Net, material, Z/vacuum,
port, EPR, and run-control inputs; unset or unknown values stay explicit. It
does no file I/O, meshing, catalogue rebuild, or native solver inspection and
does not claim native geometry or run evidence.
For the source summary, `source.top_cell_name` uses a valid adapter-selected
`selected_cell_name` first, then falls back to legacy `top_cell_name` when the
selected name is unavailable, and otherwise is `None`. This display choice
does not mutate source metadata or reread the GDS.

Its notebook HTML presents source, backend, route, and count cards, followed by
Entity/occurrence/Net/material/source-Z, port/host/direction, junction A/B/L/C,
analysis-choice, film/loss/source/margin-assumption, and solver/resource
tables. The original detached JSON is in a collapsed disclosure. Unknown
values remain distinct from zero; `None` means all and an empty tuple means
none only for a selection, while an absent request is labeled not requested.
The HTML has no theme
argument and inherits the front-end light/dark palette; the detached `.data`
contract is unchanged.


## Physical declarations, for PDK authors {#physical-declarations}

A PDK declares how each film or volume is classified; SCGSim never infers it
from names, Nets, materials, sizes or equal heights. One LayerStack assembly
frame and one physical layer identity per film are shared across its Entities,
polygons and child occurrences, and placement applies once before the profile
is interpreted. A physical declaration distinguishes stack films, local films
and finite volumes. Original material, normal film thickness, attachment face,
source interval, Entity identity, polygon holes and actual body endpoints stay
source facts: a finite volume's nominal layer interval does not replace an
individual body's interval, and a TSV wall's radial thickness is not its axial
span.

One physical representation plan holds the selected profile, the source to
effective coordinate trace, the per-body representation, the support
projection and the complete enclosure mapping. Palace and AEDT read that plan;
backend construction, Nets, ports, junctions, RLC treatments and numerical
controls keep their own owners. A stack film is removed once per physical
identity; a local film is projected to its authored attachment face without
removing thickness from unrelated intervals; retained volumes map their actual
endpoints; and the requested enclosure maps once.

Contact and host incidence remain source records. Missing qualified incidence
stays missing; it does not block physical lowering, and a consumer that needs
it reports that limitation instead of guessing. Source contact normals do not
establish HFSS calculator Surface or Adjacent field sides or native electrical
continuity.

### The typed source carrier {#typed-source-carrier-and-plan}

The source owner's `LayerLevel.info["physical_layer"]` contains the serialized
neutral declaration. Preserve all original Level arguments and existing info
when adding that carrier; no solver target material is written into it.

```python
from gdsfactory.technology import LayerLevel
from scgsim.geometry.models.physical import (
    ApproximationProfile, PhysicalLayerDeclaration, PhysicalRepresentationPlan,
)
from scgsim.geometry.interpretation.physical import interpret_physical_geometry

declaration = PhysicalLayerDeclaration.from_payload(authored_declaration)
level = LayerLevel(
    **authored_level_arguments,  # existing source arguments, excluding info
    info={**authored_level_info, "physical_layer": declaration.to_payload()},
)
profile = ApproximationProfile("thin_film", "v1", {})
effective_input, effective_stack, plan = interpret_physical_geometry(
    normalized_source_input, source_stack, profile,
)
recorded_plan = plan.to_payload()
read_plan = PhysicalRepresentationPlan.from_payload(recorded_plan)
body = read_plan.map_body(
    declared_physical_layer_id, actual_source_interval_um, original_source_geometry,
)
```

`PhysicalLayerDeclaration` has these exact fields:

- `physical_layer_id`, `source_level_id`, `source_level_and_gds_pair` and
  `source_interval_um`: source identity, selector association and nominal span.
- `material_id` and `feature_kind`: original material and `stack_film`,
  `local_film` or `finite_volume` classification.
- `physical_dimensions`: source normal film thickness or finite-volume facts;
  radial wall thickness and axial span remain distinct.
- `source_contact_facts`: authored attachment face and available source normals.
- `actual_entity_contact_graph`: the existing authored graph, or `None` when
  unavailable. Process-connectivity descriptions are not qualified placed
  footprint/contact proof.

The plan uses schema `scgsim.geometry.physical-representation.v1`. Its tagged
payload records the explicit profile, source identity, declarations, collapse
intervals, sheet anchors, per-Entity facts and complete enclosure traces.
`context` projects those facts for shared planning; `map_body()`,
`project_support_point()` and `project_enclosure()` supply consumer projections
without a second profile interpreter.

The declaration's original `material_id` stays source identity. Native AEDT
PEC material or Perfect E/ThinConductor assignments are backend realization
and separately observed evidence; they never replace that source identity.

### Selected declarations and source incidence {#selected-declarations-and-source-incidence}

A declaration catalogue is not the selected model. Only the physical levels
the selected source binds are read; an unused catalogue film does not create a
collapse event. The selected bridge assembly supplies qualified M1-to-substrate,
post-to-Ground and deck-to-post source incidence; preserve those records and
their body and occurrence ownership. They establish source incidence, not
native continuity or HFSS field-side proof. Generic bridge and bump incidence
stays unavailable where it is not authored, and missing records are neither
invented nor made prerequisites for physical lowering.

### Older layer records {#fresh-and-historical-layer-records}

Fresh physical-source preparation consumes neutral `PhysicalLayerDeclaration`
records and an explicit `ApproximationProfile`. Fresh `aedt_modeling` metadata
and role-derived route classification are not adapters. A request
payload with `PhysicalLayerSpec` records and no tagged representation was
written by an earlier SCGSim and is refused; a new physical-source execution
requires neutral declarations.
Explicit Solid bodies without layer declarations retain their finite source
geometry through the shared identity plan, without minted physical IDs.

The selected plan's tagged payload is the current prepared physical trace. A
prepared geometry whose trace is untagged (a `PhysicalLayerSpec` layer map) was
written by an earlier SCGSim and is refused with a replacement preparation
instruction; read it with the SCGSim commit that wrote it.

### Profile bindings {#profile-bindings}

The source-authorized bindings of `substrate_face` and `metal_gap_equivalent`
identify actual normalized supporting Entities and their `lower` or `upper`
faces; they are not reconstructed from layer names, roles or equal Z values.
`set_route()` takes no keyword that repeats the profile's name and does not
author bindings or own coordinate arithmetic. `build_route_geometry()` requires
preparation's effective normalized input and representation context. Use
neutral declarations with `interpret_physical_layers()` or
`interpret_physical_geometry()`.

## Calls below the supported entry {#supported-entry}

A layout enters SCGSim through the public API: `GeometryPlan` and the
simulation classes of `scgsim.palace` and `scgsim.aedt`. The rules, the
guarantees and the owners on this page are stated for a layout that enters
this way.

SCGSim also documents one API below that entry, and you can call it with an
input you build by hand: `scgsim.geometry.sgb.build_sgb_geometry`, the
geometry builder, with a `GeometryBuildInput` you construct yourself, in place
of the one a `GeometryPlan` snapshot carries.

Functions inside this package that take lower-level records, such as a prism
catalogue (SGB's own list of footprints, each extruded over a height range),
are internal and are not a documented API.

Calling this API with an input you build is internal or advanced use, and
**its precondition is what the supported entry guarantees**: the input is one
that `GeometryPlan` and a simulation class could have produced. It starts after
the checks those two make and does not repeat them. A direct call to
`build_sgb_geometry` runs
neither the plan checks of `GeometryPlan` nor the meshing-stage check of
`mesh()` and `simulation_drc()`.

An input that only this API can build is not a supported use. For such an
input SCGSim promises only this:

- If it gives a plausible but wrong result without an error, and a cheap check
  where the input enters can refuse it clearly, SCGSim adds that check.
- Otherwise SCGSim states the precondition once, where the API is documented,
  or records the case and leaves the behavior as it is.

When a direct call fails or returns something you did not expect, build the
same layout through `GeometryPlan` and a simulation class before you report
it. The rules and owners on this page apply to that build.


## Lumped-port sheets on the grid {#lumped-port-lattice}

How a lumped-port sheet becomes a rectangle is stated for users on
[Lumped ports are made rectangles](../../reference/supported-geometry.qmd#lumped-port-rectangle).
This is the derivation behind it.

### The rectangle {#lumped-port-angle}

A rectangle whose four corners are grid points runs along a direction of whole
grid steps: its side along the port is k steps of v = (p, q), where p and q are
whole numbers with no common factor, and its side across the port is m steps of
(−q, p). This v is the port's direction on the grid: (1, 0) or (0, 1) along x or
y, (1, 1) at 45°, and (3, 4) for a side that runs 3 grid steps in x for every 4
in y. SCGSim reads each sheet as such a rectangle:

1. **Its four corners.** Where a conductor outline crosses a side of the sheet,
   the grid rounds the crossing to a grid point; on a side at an angle that
   point can lie off the side by up to half a grid diagonal (0.71 nm on a 1 nm
   grid), the grid's snap bound. SCGSim drops every vertex that lies within the
   snap bound of the line between the two corners of its side and keeps the four
   corners. When a vertex lies so close to a corner that more than one set of
   four vertices passes this rule, SCGSim reads each set as in step 2 and keeps
   the one whose rectangle lies nearest its drawn corners; when two lie equally
   near, SCGSim refuses the port and names both.
2. **The rectangle.** When the four corners as drawn are grid points of such a
   rectangle, nothing moves. Otherwise, for example when an instance registered
   with a `GeometryPlan` and turned by 45° places a sheet drawn along x, so that
   its corners leave the grid, SCGSim takes the nearest such rectangle whose
   corners each lie within the snap bound of the drawn corners, and records how
   far each corner moved. When there is none, or the nearest one does not run
   along the port direction, SCGSim refuses the port, naming it, its layer and
   its four drawn corners in µm. A layout passed whole, without a plan, reaches
   SCGSim with its corners already on the grid; they are its drawn corners.

Between the two cuts, the sheet's long sides are the sides of that rectangle, so
the port is exactly the rectangle. Beyond the cuts, the end pieces keep the
vertices the grid shares with the conductors.

### The cuts {#lumped-port-cuts}

A cut across the rectangle has both its ends on grid points only every
|v| = √(p² + q²) grid steps along the port: at every grid step along x or y,
every 1.414 nm at 45° on a 1 nm grid, and every 5 nm along (3, 4). These are the
cut positions. On each end, SCGSim chooses the cut in two steps:

1. It starts at the first cut position, at or past the conductor's farthest
   reach into the sheet, that leaves one connected end piece: the largest
   rectangle the sheet holds.
2. The end piece adds an edge to its conductor along each long side of the
   sheet, from where the conductor's outline meets that side to the cut. The
   cut moves one cut position further into the gap at a time until each such
   edge is zero or at least 10 grid steps long (10 nm on a 1 nm grid), so the
   side wall that stands on it is not narrower than the fine-structure limit for
   side walls. Where the conductor's own edge already runs along the side, the
   end piece continues that edge and adds none.

A gap that holds fewer than two cut positions has no room for the rectangle:
SCGSim refuses the port and names where the gap lies, its length and the cut
spacing.

The outline is the one SGB builds: a conductor declared with an exact arc meets
the side where the arc does, on the grid point SGB rounds the crossing to, not
where its polygon does, and reaches into the sheet as far as the arc does, also
where a chord of its polygon faces the sheet. SCGSim reads that outline from
SGB's own binding of the conductor's boundary records, so a record on a port's
conductor is refused as it is on any other conductor: with the same
`InputError` and the same message. Binding a record needs the model grid the
input declares, which `GeometryPlan` always declares. A sheet that ends on straight conductor edges at right
angles to it keeps the face and the conductors it had: its cuts lie on those
edges and its end pieces are empty.

For the circular pad coupon (pad radius 100 µm in a ground opening of radius
120 µm, a 2 µm sheet, 1 nm grid):

| End | The outline meets the sheet sides at | Largest rectangle | Cut taken | Edge added |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pad, arc of radius 100 µm | x = 99.995 µm | x = 100.000 µm, edge 5 nm | x = 100.005 µm | 10 nm |
| Ground opening, arc of radius 120 µm | x = 119.996 µm | x = 119.988 µm, edge 8 nm | x = 119.986 µm | 10 nm |

The port is 19.981 µm long, 0.007 µm shorter than the largest rectangle.

### Worked example: the Xmon's junction port at 45° {#lumped-port-xmon}

The [flip-chip Xmon](../../guides/xmon/inputs.qmd) draws its junction sheet at 45°
across the gap between the ground opening and the Xmon pad, on a 1 nm grid. On
the grid the sheet has eight vertices, four of them added where the two round
outlines cross its long sides:

| Vertex | Position (µm) | Read as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | (−55.443, −24.420) | corner |
| | (−54.742, −23.719) | on side AB, where the ground opening crosses it: dropped |
| | (−52.143, −21.120) | on side AB, where the Xmon pad crosses it: dropped |
| B | (−51.443, −20.420) | corner |
| C | (−51.633, −20.230) | corner |
| | (−52.333, −20.930) | on side CD, where the Xmon pad crosses it: dropped |
| | (−54.933, −23.529) | 0.707 nm outside side CD, half a grid diagonal, where the ground opening crosses it: dropped |
| D | (−55.633, −24.230) | corner |

- **Direction.** B − A = (4000, 4000) nm = 4000 · (1, 1), so v = (1, 1) and the
  cut positions are √2 nm = 1.414 nm apart.
- **Width.** D − A = (−190, 190) nm = 190 · (−1, 1): the port is
  190 · √2 nm = 268.70 nm wide, as drawn.
- **Shift.** The four corners are grid points of a rectangle, so none moves. The
  recorded shifts, below 10⁻¹⁴ µm, are the floating-point rounding of placing
  the cell.
- **Cuts.** Counted in cut positions from A:

| End | Largest rectangle | Edge added | Cut taken | Edge added |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ground opening, at A | 708, 1.0013 µm from A | 9.9 nm | 709, 1.0027 µm from A | 11.3 nm |
| Xmon pad, at B | 3292, 4.6556 µm from A | 11.3 nm | 3292 | 11.3 nm |

The cut at 709 ends at (−54.734, −23.711) and (−54.924, −23.521) µm, the cut at
3292 at (−52.151, −21.128) and (−52.341, −20.938) µm: these are the port's four
corners. The port is 2583 · √2 nm = 3.6529 µm long, and SGB builds its face with
an area of 0.98154 µm².

### What SCGSim records {#lumped-port-record}

The partition record of each port carries what SCGSim did under `lattice`:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `direction_grid` | v = (p, q), the port's direction in whole grid steps |
| `cut_spacing_um` | the distance between cut positions, \|v\| grid steps |
| `corners_um` | the rectangle's corners A, B, C and D: A starts the port on its right-hand side, B = A + k v ends it |
| `drawn_corners_um` | the corners as drawn, before the grid rounded them |
| `corner_shifts_um` | how far each corner moved from its drawn corner, in x and y |
| `cuts` | each cut's `index` (cut positions from A), `from_corner_a_um` and its two `ends_um` |
| `modelled_sheet_um` | the sheet with its long sides straight between the cuts, present only when they were not |

The partition records it in the prepared input as
`metadata["junction_partitions"][junction_id]["lattice"]`, and the SGB model
Palace and AEDT both solve is built from that record. A Palace simulation keeps
it on the port sheet of its prepared geometry, under
`rectangular_junction_lattice`.
